items.title: Daryl Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 11, 2024
items.q: My father, Sammy, was a trombonist... that was my first most important mentorship.

ctx.x: He’s decomposing. Okay I want to take you back a bit and I’m going to do that by seeing if you can name this tune. All right? I’ll give it my best rendition. [scats]

[sings] “perhaps someone else may be nearer/your heart.” Interesting that you should do that one. It’s not one — it’s not necessarily a staple that I have played throughout, and I’m not even sure I can recall that many people asking for it, but it was a song that I sang a lot in my home in Woonsocket, Rhode Island, and I probably heard it on the radio or on the many recordings that my father would play. My father, Sammy, was a trombonist and although he was mainly working in our family restaurant, on the weekends…
written in the trombone bass line. But I don’t think that was one of them. The one that I remember, and I never sing it it’s too rangy, is “I’ll Get By.”
